beats.intro: The distance from Earth to the Sun is about one hundred fifty billion meters. A dust grain is about zero point zero zero zero zero five meters wide. [[q]]Numbers like these are long and easy to miscount. Scientific notation keeps them short.
beats.define: In scientific notation, a number is written as two parts multiplied together. [[first]]The first part is at least one and less than ten. [[second]]The second part is a power of ten. [[ex]]For example, five point seven times ten to the sixth. [[mean]]Ten to the sixth is one million, so this is five point seven million: five million seven hundred thousand.
beats.big: To write a large number in scientific notation, [[q]]take eight million seven hundred ten thousand. [[hop]]Move the decimal point to the left until only one digit is in front of it. [[count]]That took six hops. [[res]]So the number is eight point seven one times ten to the sixth. [[why]]Each hop to the left divides by ten, and the ten to the sixth multiplies it back.
beats.small: Small numbers work the same way, in the other direction. [[q]]Take zero point zero zero zero zero nine two three eight four. [[hop]]Move the decimal point to the right until one nonzero digit is in front of it. [[count]]That took five hops. [[res]]So it's nine point two three eight four times ten to the negative five. [[rule]]A number of ten or more gets a positive exponent. A number less than one gets a negative exponent.
beats.q1: Quick check. Write in scientific notation.
beats.back: Going back to standard form reverses the hops. [[q]]One point two nine times ten to the fifth: [[hop]]a positive exponent, so move the point five places to the right, filling in zeros. [[res]]That's one hundred twenty-nine thousand. [[q2]]And nine point zero four two times ten to the negative three: [[hop2]]a negative exponent, so move the point three places to the left. [[res2]]That's zero point zero zero nine zero four two.
beats.q2: Quick check. Write in standard form.
beats.compare: Scientific notation makes comparing easy. [[q]]Which is larger: four times ten to the negative three, or two point seven times ten to the negative five? [[exp]]Compare the exponents first. Negative three is greater than negative five, [[ans]]so four times ten to the negative three is larger, [[scale]]about a hundred times larger, even though two point seven looks smaller than four.
beats.wrap: Scientific notation is a number from one up to ten, times a power of ten. [[w1]]Count the hops of the decimal point to find the exponent. [[w2]]Big numbers get a positive exponent, and numbers less than one get a negative exponent. [[w3]]To compare, look at the exponents first. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
